title: Platform systems & services: team wiki, runbooks, dashboards, how-tos, and roadmap
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This page consolidates the Platform team’s canonical systems & services inventory, how-tos for common operational tasks, dashboards and alerting guidance, critical runbooks, retrospective cadence, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended for on-call engineers, platform owners, and new joiners who need a single entry point for operational knowledge.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-remediate for platform incidents; provide consistent runbooks and dashboards; make roadmap priorities and team responsibilities discoverable.
- Scope: Hosting, routing, inference gateways, autoscaling controllers, cache layers (Redis/Memcached), batch workers, metrics/trace/logging pipelines, CI/CD used for platform services, and observability artifacts (Grafana, Alertmanager).

Owners and contacts
- Platform team lead: Aisha Patel (owner)
- On-call rotation: eng-platform-oncall (primary) — see rota in PagerDuty group: PD-ENG-PLATFORM
- Escalation path:
  1. On-call engineer (primary)
  2. Platform pager (secondary)
  3. Service owner (contact in the Systems Inventory below)
  4. Engineering manager / SRE lead (for severity >= Sev2)

Service inventory (high-level)
- inference-gateway (Kubernetes: namespace=redwood-inference): routes external traffic, implements auth, rate-limiting. Owner: inference-service-owner@redwood.com
- model-runtime (Kubernetes GPU pool): long-running inference pods (dedicated & hosted). Owner: runtime-team@redwood.com
- batch-encoder (Kubernetes): batch embedding jobs / offline pipelines. Owner: data-platform@redwood.com
- kv-cache (Redis cluster): prefix and KV caches for model context. Owner: infra-caching@redwood.com
- observability-stack (Grafana, Prometheus, Tempo, Loki): metrics/traces/logs. Owner: eng-platform-observability@redwood.com

SLOs & alerts guidance
- Latency SLOs (inference gateway):
  - p50 < 40ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms (for small text gen workload).
  - Error budget: 99.95% availability per calendar month.
- Error SLOs: request-level 5xx rate < 0.1% (global).
- Alert thresholds (recommended):
  - High latency: p95 > 250ms for 5m -> P1 alert to on-call.
  - Elevated error rate: 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m -> P1.
  - Sustained reduced capacity: pods_ready < desired_replicas - 2 for 2m -> P2.
  - Redis slowlog spikes (>50 ops >100ms in 1m) -> P2.
  - Prometheus remote_write failures (rate > 0.1 for 10m) -> P2.
- Alert policy notes:
  - Avoid noisy alerts by using rolling-window aggregation (5m) and anomaly-suppressing silence during deploys.
  - Send P1 alerts to PagerDuty with a runbook link and heartbeat checks enabled.

Dashboards (recommended panels)
- inference-gateway – Global overview (Grafana):
  - QPS (requests/s) with model variant breakdown
  - Latency histogram and p50/p95/p99 heatmap
  - 5xx/4xx rates by route
  - Active connections / inflight requests
  - Token generation rate and average tokens/request
- model-runtime – GPU pool dashboard:
  - GPU utilization per node (util%, mem%)
  - Pod-level vram usage and GPU mig partitions
  - Batch queue length and queue latency
  - Node-level temperature / ECC errors (if available)
- kv-cache dashboard:
  - Cache hit ratio over time (recommended target >85%)
  - Eviction rate and memory usage by slot
  - Slow commands and CLUSTER SLOTS rebalancing operations
- CI/CD pipeline dashboards:
  - Recent deploys, rollback counts, deploy duration, and failure rate

Example Grafana queries (PromQL)
- QPS (per route): sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-gateway"}[1m])) by (route)
- p95 latency (ms): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-gateway"}[5m])) by (le)) * 1000
- Redis hits: 100 * (sum(rate(redis_keyspace_hits_total[5m])) / (sum(rate(redis_keyspace_hits_total[5m])) + sum(rate(redis_keyspace_misses_total[5m]))))

How-tos (short procedural guides)
1) Add a dashboard panel
  - Step 1: Open Grafana (grafana.internal.redwood.com) -> Dashboard -> Import / New panel.
  - Step 2: Use the recommended query from the panel library (see below) and set visualization to gauge/heatmap as appropriate.
  - Step 3: Add panel thresholds to match SLOs (example: p95 latency threshold = 200ms).
  - Step 4: Save to folder: Platform / inference-gateway and add the panel to the Observability checklist PR.

2) Create a Prometheus alert rule
  - Step 1: Create or edit rule file under Git repo: infra/observability/alerts/alerts-inference.yaml
  - Step 2: Follow existing rule format and include annotations: summary, runbook (link), severity. Example snippet:

    - alert: InferenceHighP95Latency
      expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"inference-gateway\"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.25
      for: 5m
      labels:
        severity: P1
      annotations:
        summary: "Inference gateway p95 latency > 250ms"
        runbook: "confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-team-wiki-playbooks-runbooks-roadmap-2026-q3#runbook---inference-degradation"

  - Step 3: Submit PR to infra/observability and tag @eng-platform-observability for review.
  - Step 4: After merge, validate firing in staging then promote to prod alertmanager.

Runbooks (critical incident playbooks)
Runbook — Inference Degradation (P1)
- Symptoms:
  - Sudden increase in p95 latency, increased 5xx errors, client-side timeouts.
- Immediate steps (0–10 minutes):
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty and post to #incident-platform with incident template.
  2. Check global dashboard: Grafana -> inference-gateway overview.
  3. Confirm if the issue is traffic-related: run:
     - kubectl -n redwood-inference get hpa,deploy,sts
     - kubectl -n redwood-inference top pods | sort -rk3 | head -n 10
     - curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} \n" 'https://inference-gateway.internal/healthz'
  4. If pods are OOM/killed, run: kubectl describe pod <pod> and kubectl logs <pod> --previous.
- Mitigation (10–30 minutes):
  1. If autoscaler is not scaling: inspect HPA controller logs and metrics-server health. Temporarily scale deployment: kubectl -n redwood-inference scale deploy inference-gateway --replicas=5 (restore after root cause).
  2. If Redis is saturated: failover to read-only replica or increase maxmemory (follow couch of infra-cache runbook).
  3. If a model variant is causing errors: add route-level fallback to a stable variant via routing-policy config: kubectl edit cm routing-policy -n redwood-config and update fallback rules.
- Recovery validation (30–60 minutes):
  1. Monitor p95 and 5xx for 30 minutes, confirm stable under thresholds.
  2. Post incident notes in incident tracker and assign postmortem owner.

Runbook — Deploy rollback (P2)
- Trigger: deploy causes increased errors or latency and quick fix needed.
- Steps:
  1. Identify offending deploy in CI: check deploy tag and pipeline logs.
  2. Rollback using kubectl rollout undo deploy/<name> -n <ns> --to-revision=<rev> OR trigger rollback job in ArgoCD.
  3. Verify traffic returns to normal and no leftover broken config remains.

Retention, postmortem, and retrospectives
- Postmortem policy: All Sev1/Sev2 incidents require a written postmortem within 72 hours and a retrospective meeting within 7 business days.
- Template requirements: timeline, impact, root cause, contributing factors, action items (owner and due date), monitoring gaps, and any follow-ups.
- Retro cadence: Monthly platform retro + quarterly cross-team retro with runtime, infra, and product.

Roadmap & upcoming work (next 6 months)
- Q2 2026 priorities:
  - Observability: migrate key dashboards to unified Grafana folder structure and add synthetic canaries for latency and correctness.
  - Autoscaling: implement multi-dimensional autoscaling for GPU nodes (cpu, queue depth, and GPU utilization).
  - Runbooks: add playbooks for quantization service and model cache eviction events.
  - Reliability: target 99.97% for hosted inference top-tier customers (pilot).
  - Developer experience: add one-click dashboard PR template and observability checklists in quickstarts.

Team wiki & contribution guide
- Where to edit: this page is stored as JSON in the confluence repo and is canonical. For operational artifacts (dashboards, alerts, runbooks) prefer PRs to infra/observability or docs/platform and tag @eng-platform.
- Minimal PR checklist for changes that impact alerts or runbooks:
  1. Link to dashboard/alert rule and explain rationale.
  2. Include test plan (how to validate in staging).
  3. Add reviewer: @eng-platform-observability and @eng-sre on call.
  4. Update this wiki page’s change-log section.

Appendix: useful commands & snippets
- Check gateway health: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} \n" 'https://inference-gateway.internal/healthz'
- List failing pods: kubectl -n redwood-inference get pods --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
- Tail logs by label: kubectl -n redwood-inference logs -l app=inference-gateway -f
- Force rotate Redis primary (run with infra-cache owner): redis-cli -h <host> -p <port> CLUSTER FAILOVER FORCE

Change log
